page_title: About my garden or observation space
introduction: Begin with a simple description. You can update this page as your understanding grows.
observation_challenge: Choose one garden, balcony, yard, community garden, or nearby green space that you can revisit during the course.

introduction: Connect current conditions with patterns you have noticed over time.
observation_challenge: Spend a few minutes observing one part of your garden. Notice what is happening today before trying to explain why.

introduction: Notice the variety of living things in and around your garden.
observation_challenge: Observe quietly for 10 minutes. Look from the soil surface to flowers, shrubs, and tree canopies.

introduction: Compare soil conditions and look for signs of soil health.
observation_challenge: Compare soil in two locations. Notice texture, moisture, surface cover, compaction, roots, and visible organisms.

introduction: Notice where water collects, runs off, soaks in, or disappears quickly.
observation_challenge: After rain or irrigation, compare two areas and look for differences in water movement and soil moisture.

introduction: Use evidence from your observations to consider one manageable change.
observation_challenge: Review earlier entries and look for a repeated observation, concern, or opportunity.

introduction: Your journal can continue after the course ends.
observation_challenge: Review the complete journal and identify the observations that most influenced your thinking.
